description:
ENFORCEMENT LAYER: reliability moves from memorized-instruction to HARNESS-OWNED triggers that carry self-contained instructions at the moment of action. Proven principle: cron survives compaction because the cron prompt is fresh input re-injected AFTER the wipe (the agent does not remember; the trigger re-tells it). Same property makes hooks reliable (harness-fired, not model-fired).

VERIFIED HOOK MAPPING (docs pulled 2026-05-22, code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks):
- PreToolUse on Bash (e.g. git commit): hard mechanical gate via exit 2 / permissionDecision:deny. FULLY DETERMINISTIC, no model in loop, COMPACTION-IMMUNE. For: author-field audit, clean-tree-before-branch, no -m in bw comment.
- Stop: inject additionalContext (self-check "did you do A,B,C?") + exit 2 to force rework before the turn can end. Caveat: Claude can commit BEFORE Stop fires and may stop mid-question - so pre-action gates belong on PreToolUse, not Stop.
- PostToolUse on the Agent tool: fires in the PARENT context when a sub-agent returns; injects "sub-agent done - run the checker against its output". (SubagentStop CANNOT inject additionalContext - verified - so use PostToolUse-on-Agent for the check-a-sub-agent pattern.)
- cron: periodic poll; survives compaction by fresh re-injection. For standing checks.

KEY LIMIT: hooks CANNOT directly dispatch a sub-agent (verified). They inject the instruction + block the turn so the dispatch is non-optional; the model still issues it. Strong, not absolute -> the peer-checker backstop matters.

CHECKER AGENT: judgment backstop, triggered by a hook. Orchestrator-fired (a leaf agent cannot dispatch a checker - can't-nest). Cross-check (each other's work) > self-check (shared blind spots). Fills a real gap: orchestrator OUTPUTS (activation pastes, arc-closes, commits, directives) currently have no checker.

DETECTION of compaction-derailment: do NOT try to detect "compaction happened". Detect "output diverges from bw ground truth" - the checking layer IS the derailment detector (a derailed agent produces non-conforming output regardless of cause). A derailed agent cannot self-detect; detection must be external + comparison-based vs durable bw. Ready-made canary: the bw seat-tag convention (operating-disciplines 7.7) - a dropped/mistagged [from: seat] tag is a cheap signal. Bounded by check cadence (one cron/peer cycle, not instant).

REMEDIATION: re-decompose the failed unit into smaller pieces and re-dispatch (orchestrator job - can't-nest). Compaction-derailment correlates with task size; small-enough tasks never compact. System self-tunes granularity (prevention by sizing small up front + reaction by splitting; the reaction TEACHES the prevention). bw-as-memory makes fine decomposition cheap (state read from bw, not carried in-head, so splits don't fragment context). GUARDRAILS: (1) checker must distinguish size-derail (split) from wrong-spec/blocked/impossible (escalate, do NOT split) else infinite subdivision; (2) attempt cap -> escalate to human; (3) granularity floor (too-small = handoff/coordination overhead). Slots into the existing MAJOR_PLINY 5.6 INCOMPLETE/UNVERIFIABLE verdict protocol.

AUTHORING RULE for every trigger payload (cron AND hook additionalContext): state WHY it fired and WHAT to do, self-contained inline (not "see 5.1.3" - a pointer fails after compaction).

VERIFY AT BUILD TIME: PostCompact reportedly cannot inject context (per docs pulled) - so no immediate auto-reprime the instant compaction finishes; the next trigger carries it. Re-confirm against the live version (hook surfaces shift).
